text:
sam: FYI saw a sharp write-latency spike on several hosts during a GPU slot eviction batch, starting ~2045012300. Affects tail latency for short gen jobs.
ops-bot: alert: nvme_write_latency: host-set-a increased 99th from 12ms -> 250ms over 3m :warning:
chris: which hosts? I can pull iostat and the nvme SMART.
sam: hosts: ip-10-2-11-7, ip-10-2-11-9, ip-10-2-12-3. Pattern: eviction coincides with ephemeral cleaner running + concurrent scratch GC.
talia: any disk errors in dmesg? Could be write amplification from scrub + GC.
sam: quick paste from ip-10-2-11-7: ```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device             r/s     w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s  r_await  w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1           12.00  820.00   48.00  820.00   0.00    0.00    1.25    98.40   0.90  82.96
```
chris: that w_await is brutal. 98ms for writes. Are we running the scrub concurrently with eviction? Which cleaner seed?
sam: cleaner job id f9c3e; autoscaler scheduled evictions to free GPUs for higher-tier jobs. Cleaner triggered because ephemeral usage hit 92%.
riley: we recently bumped cleaner concurrency from 2 -> 6 to speed reclaiming. Might be too aggressive with background write IO. Suggest rolling back to 2 and adding IO caps.
talia: agree. Also check if kernel writeback backlog spikes. Can we throttle cleaner with ionice/blkio?
chris: we have a per-host systemd unit for ephemeral-cleaner. Suggest adding `--max-write-kbps=20480` and `ionice -c2 -n7` as mitigation. Also propose staging drain window to avoid scheduling eviction during scrub.
sam: running a quick test patch on canary (ip-10-2-11-7): cleaner concurrency -> 2 and `--max-write-kbps=16384`. I'll observe for 30m.
ops-bot: deploy: ephemeral-cleaner@canary restarted by sam at 2045012560
sam: preliminary: 99th write latency dropped to ~18ms after limiting. No full SMART errors. No signs of firmware errors.
riley: longer term: we should change scheduler policy to prefer draining hosts with <70% ephemeral. Also add a pre-eviction hook that checks active scrub/GC.
talia: open an RFC? We need: 1) revert cleaner concurrency to 2, 2) add IO cap by default, 3) scheduler pre-check, 4) monitoring alert tweak to correlate cleaner runs with write-latency spikes.
chris: I'll draft the rollout plan. Minimal immediate action: keep canary limits for 2h, then roll to 20% of fleet. If stable, full roll.
sam: thanks. Posting logs to the incident thread and will follow up with perf graphs. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: note: incident ticket INF-4312 created (storage:cleaner-io-spike)
